title: Binary search on sorted arrays — k closest, then distinct values in a huge array
label: single
statement: Given a **sorted** array, an integer `k` and a target `x`, return the **k elements closest to `x`**, in ascending order. On a tie in distance, prefer the smaller element.
provenance: Two LinkedIn onsite questions from Aug 2026 (FastPrep): "Find K closest elements in a sorted array" (LeetCode 658) and "Count distinct values in a huge sorted array". The second has no public statement; stage 2 is my reading of it.

sources.name: FastPrep — LinkedIn interview questions, dated reports 2024–2026

stages.title: K closest elements
stages.say: Return the k elements closest to x from a sorted array.

stages.title: Distinct values in a huge array
stages.say: The sorted array has billions of entries but few distinct values. Count them without reading every element.
stages.require: Add `SortedSearch.CountDistinct(a)`: O(d log n) for d distinct values.

prompts.label: Check my design — no code
prompts.text: I believe binary-search the left edge of the k-wide answer window by comparing the elements just outside it — O(log(n−k) + k); for distinct values, binary-search the end of each run so the cost depends on the number of distinct values, not the length. Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Given a **sorted** array, an integer `k` and a target `x`, return the **k elements closest to `x`**, in ascending order. On a tie in distance, prefer the smaller element.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Ties: smaller element wins? (Yes.)
- k larger than the array? (Throw.)
- Return sorted? (Yes.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: The answer is always a contiguous window of length k. Binary-search its left edge: if x is farther from arr[mid] than from arr[mid + k], the window must start further right.

learn.title: 4 · Approach
learn.md: I would say, before coding: "B."inary-search the left edge of the k-wide answer window by comparing the elements just outside it — O(log(n−k) + k); for distinct values, binary-search the end of each run so the cost depends on the number of distinct values, not the length."

learn.title: 11 · AI usage strategy
learn.md:
- Make the design decision yourself, then ask the assistant to attack it.
- Delegate the mechanical parts only after the structure is fixed.

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Sorting by distance (O(n log n)) and ignoring that the input is sorted.
- A heap of size k — fine, but not the intended O(log n).
- Breaking ties toward the larger element.
- int overflow computing distances.
